summary.intent: Assess whether Phase 72 needed discussion before planning, audit stale/pending todos for drift from Phases 70/70.1/71, then plan, execute, and ship Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability/correctness) while resolving unrelated CI regressions discovered along the way.
summary.outcome: Diagnosed and fixed three CI regressions (FUSE seq-1 equivocation, stale desktop-e2e DTO fields, web-e2e rotation-durability floor store, sdk-e2e Test 21 flake, plus web-e2e timing flakes) across merged PRs #600 and #601; retired 8 stale Phase 71 todos and folded 2 new ones into Phases 72/73; completed Phase 72 research, pattern-mapping, and planning (10 plans/8 waves), and got through Wave 0-1 of execution with a new hardening plan (72-11) added to fix vitest v2→v3 Mock-type drift in test files and wire test-inclusive typechecking into CI.

repo: GSD repo closes todos by deleting from pending/ and adding to completed/ (via git mv) — an empty resolved/ folder is a red herring; check completed/ instead

ci-e2e.yml (Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on PRs — must dispatch manually via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`, which 422s on older workflow definitions) to validate before merge

Playwright web-e2e ciFloor() helper only raises wait timeouts to 60s under CI env; locally waits stay at their bare value (15-30s), causing local-only flakes on IPNS-gated ops that pass fine in CI — local verification requires CI=1 plus patching webServer.reuseExistingServer (normally `!process.env.CI`) to avoid port conflicts

Root `pnpm typecheck` in CI only runs tsconfig.build.json (excludes tests) — test files are never typechecked in CI, allowing vitest v2→v3 Mock<> generic drift (50+ errors in sdk-core) to go undetected since it's runtime-green under vitest's transpile-only test execution

Phase 71 (#599) shipped with three separate pieces of undetected test/fixture drift: stale desktop-e2e .mts DTO field names (readDescriptorRef→encryptedReadKey, rootIpnsName→shareRootIpnsName), an sdk-e2e Test 21 assertion that didn't account for its own idempotency, and it exposed a FUSE seq=1 equivocation bug

Phase 70.1 collapsed IndexedDB stores generation-high-water + seq-high-water into a single rotation-floor store (DB cipherbox-rotation-state v2, keyed by nodeId) but left an e2e test helper pointed at the old store names

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on the first-publish branch gated only by 'inode cid empty'; a dropped/stale UploadComplete re-running it re-seals with a new CID at seq=1, tripping Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate. Fixed by resolving IPNS first via resolve_ipns_for_replay and routing Found outcomes into the existing CAS retry path instead of skipping.

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param (Greptile P2 fix) so the Found path from content_ops.rs doesn't redundantly re-resolve sequence; conflict-retry path still re-resolves since a pre-resolved value is stale after a conflict.

Test 4.10 (Batch delete) and 4.11 (Batch move) use bare 15s waitForItemToDisappear timeouts for IPNS-gated batch ops that reliably exceed 15s on local hardware even when healthy; bumped to 30s (CI still floors to 60s via ciFloor, so no CI behavior change).

Test 6.6.2's version-count gate (expect getVersionCount()===1) is a no-op since restore swaps current↔v1 leaving count at 1 both before and after — provided zero actual wait for the IPNS republish, causing the editor to read stale content. Replaced with expect.poll() re-opening the editor until content matches the expected post-restore value.

Write-plane helper duplication exists at multiple call sites (lines ~851, 2825) targeted by Phase 72 SC#6's walkChildWriteKey consolidation across 7 call-sites with divergent fail-open/fail-closed behavior — the highest-blast-radius piece of Phase 72, deferred to research+planner rather than a product decision.

workflow: When a background verification run cascades on an unrelated flaky test blocking the target tests, iteratively bumping timeouts one at a time risks whack-a-mole (each fix reveals the next tightest wait) — running once under the CI-equivalent timeout regime (CI=1) surfaces the true failure set in one pass instead

Before recommending a Greptile/CodeRabbit-flagged optimization, weigh blast radius: a valid-but-low-value fix (e.g., threading a new param through a shared helper used by multiple callers) may be worth deferring vs. immediately implementing, but here the user chose to fix it now on the same PR since scope was small (2 real callers)

When diagnosing 'is this failure caused by my change,' check whether the changed files even overlap the failing test's imports/dependencies before deep-diving — cheap early filter to distinguish pre-existing/orthogonal flakes from real regressions

For unattended/autonomous execution phases with heavy client.ts serialization, prefer sequential execution on the main tree over git-worktree parallelism to avoid pnpm-monorepo node_modules-in-worktree failures, even when the tool defaults to worktrees

friction: gh workflow run -f ref= returned HTTP 422 because the workflow file on main predated that input; required switching to --ref <branch> syntax

Local web-e2e verification repeatedly cascaded on a different flaky test each run (4.10, then 4.11, then 2.1 twice) before reaching the actual target tests (6.6.2, 8.2), costing ~5 sequential 10-20min background runs before switching to CI=1 regime

CI=1 flips playwright webServer.reuseExistingServer to false, conflicting with the already-running local API stack — required a temporary (reverted) config patch to force reuse under CI=1 for local verification

Raw hook JSON (plan:pre capability fragments) contains literal unescaped control characters inside string values, breaking both direct JSON parsing and jq/--raw extraction; required writing a custom lenient parser script to extract fragments

git commit hung for ~2 minutes during lint-staged, apparently due to a 1Password SSH signing prompt (known issue) — required verifying post-hang whether the commit actually landed rather than retrying blindly
Earlier git cat-file checks on HEAD tree contents gave inconsistent/wrong results about whether todo moves were committed, requiring a second decisive check to resolve confusion about tree state

AskUserQuestion was invoked once without enough grounding, forcing the user to ask 'is there anything that needs to be clarified?' before the assistant did the deeper read of all 9 todos to answer definitively
